advanced.desc: Advanced selling instruments in ZhiftERP: Product Bundles — the non-stock parent, the child table, the three document behaviours, the bundle-versus-production boundary test, availability arithmetic across components, returns under the package terms, and the bundle register; blanket orders — the recorded arrangement, call-offs at approved rates through the standard chain, governance and the monthly consumption read; sales person attribution with the integrity rule and the commission boundary; Selling Settings as control-register rows with the quarterly pass; and the consolidated selling calendar assembling every read from modules 1-7 into one operating rhythm.

lessons.title: Chapter 1 — The advanced instruments: scope
lessons.html:
This final Selling module covers the instruments that extend the standard document flow: Product Bundles, blanket orders, sales person attribution and commission, and the Selling Settings that enforce the track's disciplines in configuration. It closes with the consolidated selling calendar — the operating rhythm modules 1-7 built, assembled in one place.

On completing this module you will be able to: define and operate Product Bundles including their document behaviour, availability arithmetic, and returns; set up blanket orders and manage call-offs against them; configure sales person attribution and operate the commission read within the accounting boundary; walk the Selling Settings with each setting's control-register row; and run the selling function's full calendar.

Why these instruments are a separate module. Each solves a recurring commercial situation the standard flow handles poorly:

1. The package sale — several items sold as one commercial unit at one price: without bundles, packages are assembled by hand on every document, priced inconsistently, and invoiced as component lists the customer did not buy.
2. The standing supply arrangement — agreed quantities and rates over a period, drawn down in parts: without blanket orders, each call-off renegotiates what was already agreed.
3. Attribution and reward — who sold what, and what is owed for it: without configured attribution, commission is computed outside the system from disputed spreadsheets.
4. Enforcement — the track's rules (orders before invoices, deliveries before billing, tolerances, credit postures): the settings make the rules configuration rather than memory.

Custody. Bundles and blanket arrangements are register entries with owners and reviews, per the standing register pattern; commission policy is the owner's written policy with the accountant computing payouts; settings changes are governed changes recorded in the control register (the Inventory track, module 8 pattern, extended to selling); and the calendar in Chapter 7 assigns every read this track created to its cadence and its owner.

Module contents. Chapter 2: Product Bundles — definition and document behaviour. Chapter 3: bundle operations. Chapter 4: blanket orders. Chapter 5: sales persons and commission. Chapter 6: Selling Settings. Chapter 7: the consolidated selling calendar. Chapter 8: worked example. Chapter 9: review and the module rule.

lessons.title: Chapter 2 — Product Bundles: definition and document behaviour
lessons.html:
A Product Bundle sells several items as one line. This chapter is the doctype and how documents process it.

1. The Product Bundle record. Open Product Bundle (awesome bar) > New:

1. The parent item — an Item record created for the bundle itself, flagged as a sales item but not a stock item (Maintain Stock off): the bundle is a commercial unit, not a warehoused product. Its code and name follow the register conventions; its price is set on the price lists like any item (Chapter 2.4).
2. The child table — the component items with their quantities per bundle: the stocked products that physically ship when one bundle sells.
3. The description — what prints for the bundle line, stating the package's contents per the print convention, so the customer's document says what the package contains.

2. Document behaviour. The bundle line explodes into its components where stock is involved and stays one line where money is involved:

1. On the Sales Order — the bundle enters as one row at the bundle price; the packed-items detail lists the components the row implies.
2. On the Delivery Note — the packed items drive the physical work: the components pick, their identities capture (serialised or batch components carry their numbers per the module 5 discipline), and stock deducts per component at delivery. The customer's document shows the bundle line with its packed contents.
3. On the Sales Invoice — one line at the bundle price: the customer buys one package at one price, and the invoice states exactly that. Revenue posts against the bundle line; component costs posted at delivery per component valuation — the bundle's margin is the bundle price against the summed component costs.

3. Bundles versus manufacturing. The boundary rule: a bundle is picked at despatch from components that remain ordinary stock until they ship; a manufactured or assembled product is built in advance into a new stock item through the production flow (the Manufacturing lane, where the site runs one). The test is physical: if the components are combined into a unit that sits in the warehouse as that unit, it is production; if they are gathered at picking time, it is a bundle. Choosing wrongly either creates phantom stock items nobody counts or forces production paperwork onto simple picking.

4. Pricing the bundle. The bundle's price is an Item Price on the lists like any product (module 2), moved only by the governed update. The package's commercial logic — a package price below the components' summed list prices — is stated in the bundle's register entry with the arithmetic, and the margin view reads the bundle line against its component costs at the pre-issue check like any other line.

lessons.title: Chapter 3 — Bundle operations
lessons.html:
Bundles run on the same disciplines as ordinary items, with three operational differences. This chapter states them.

1. Availability arithmetic. A bundle has no stock of its own; its availability is computed from components:

1. Sellable bundles = the minimum across components of (component available ÷ component quantity per bundle). Forty shelves and six scanners support six bundles of four-shelves-and-one-scanner, not ten.
2. The availability read — the order-time check (module 4's scheduling against stock) runs per component through the packed items: a bundle wave is at risk if any component is short, and the planning read flags the constraining component by name.
3. Replenishment — components replenish as ordinary items (the Inventory track's machinery); the bundle's forecast translates into component demand through the child quantities, and the reorder review accounts for bundle demand where bundles sell steadily.

2. Returns of bundles. Returns operate at the level that physically returns:

1. The whole package back — the return Delivery Note carries the bundle row; the packed components re-enter stock through the condition decision (module 5), each component routed on its own condition.
2. One component back (the damaged scanner from a display pack) — the return is a component-level return per the site's return configuration, with the credit or replacement sized to the component per the policy's package terms, and the package terms themselves (what a partial return does to a package price) are stated in the bundle's register entry at definition, not negotiated per case.

3. The bundle register. Each active bundle is a register row: the parent item, the components and quantities, the price arithmetic against component list totals, the package return terms, the owner, and the review date. The quarterly review (riding the pricing review) confirms: the components still current (a discontinued component makes the bundle undeliverable — the register review catches it before the order does), the price still per the decided arithmetic after component cost changes, and slow bundles retired by the item lifecycle procedure.

4. The reads. Monthly, with the sales analytics pass: bundle sales by bundle (volume and value), bundle margin (bundle revenue against component costs), and the attach effect where the register states one (the bundle's purpose — moving a slow component, anchoring a package — checked against what actually moved). The read's findings route to the register review: reprice, redefine, or retire.

lessons.title: Chapter 4 — Blanket orders
lessons.html:
A standing supply arrangement — agreed quantities and rates over a period, drawn in parts — is configured as a Blanket Order. This chapter is the doctype and its operation.

1. The Blanket Order record. Open Blanket Order (awesome bar) > New:

1. The party and period — the customer, the from and to dates of the arrangement.
2. The items table — each item with its agreed total quantity and its agreed rate for the period.
3. The order type — Selling (the same doctype serves purchasing arrangements on the other side).

The blanket order is the recorded agreement; it posts nothing, reserves nothing, and ships nothing. Its function is to hold the negotiated terms so the call-offs execute them without renegotiation.

2. Call-offs. Deliveries against the arrangement run as ordinary Sales Orders created against the blanket order:

1. The Sales Order references the blanket order; items and rates draw from it — the agreed rate applies without the deviation ladder, because the rate was approved once at the arrangement's creation (the ladder ran there, at the arrangement's size).
2. Each call-off then follows the standard flow — commitment, delivery, invoice — with all of modules 4-7's disciplines.
3. The blanket order tracks consumption: ordered quantity against the agreed total per item.

3. The arrangement's governance.

1. Creation — a blanket order is a negotiated commitment at its full value: the approval band is the ladder band of the whole arrangement, and the negotiation file (module 3's pattern) holds the versions and the approval.
2. Rate protection — the agreed rate holds for the period as the arrangement states; cost movements inside the period are the business's exposure, priced at creation (a volatile-cost item takes a shorter period or an indexation clause per the policy, decided at negotiation).
3. Amendments — quantity or rate changes mid-period are amendments to the arrangement with the same approvals as creation, per the module 4 taxonomy logic.

4. The consumption read — monthly. Active blanket orders: consumed against agreed quantity, run rate against the period's remaining time, and expiry proximity. The actions: arrangements consuming ahead of schedule route to the renewal conversation before they exhaust; arrangements far behind schedule route to the account conversation (the customer is not drawing what was agreed — the cause belongs in the file); expiring arrangements close or renew by decision, and expired rates never apply to new call-offs — a call-off after expiry is a new negotiation.

lessons.title: Chapter 5 — Sales persons and commission
lessons.html:
Attribution states who sold what; commission states what is owed for it. This chapter is the configuration and the boundary.

1. The Sales Person tree. Open Sales Person (awesome bar): the tree of selling responsibility — the sales function's people (and groups where teams share attribution), per the standing tree rules: mirror the real structure, three levels or fewer, changes by decision.

2. Attribution on documents. The sales team section on the selling documents assigns the transaction to sales persons with contribution percentages summing to one hundred:

1. Set at the order — attribution belongs to the commitment and carries to the invoice; per the policy, defaults per customer (the account's standing owner) pre-fill and are corrected only where the deal's reality differs.
2. Split attribution — shared deals carry the split the policy defines (the account owner and the closing negotiator, per the written split rules), entered at the order, not disputed at payout.
3. The integrity rule — attribution states who actually sold; it is not adjusted after the fact to move commission. Attribution changes after submission follow the amendment discipline with reasons, and the monthly read lists them.

3. Commission computation. The policy is the owner's written document: the basis (invoiced value, collected value, or margin — collected-value bases tie payout to module 7's collections and are the standing recommendation in credit-heavy books), the rates by role or band, the treatment of credits and returns (commission reverses with the value it was paid on), and the payout calendar. The system's figures feed the computation: sales by sales person from the attribution, collections from the allocation records, credits from the return documents.

4. The boundary. The selling function maintains attribution; the accountant computes and pays per the policy — through payroll or the payables lane as the policy states — and the computation file (the period's figures, the policy applied, the payout) is the accountant's record. Commission disputes resolve from the documents: the attribution on the order, the policy's written rules, the collection records — per the standing rule that disagreements resolve from records, not recollection.

5. The attribution read — monthly. Sales by sales person against the period's documents: unattributed documents (listed to zero — an unattributed sale pays nobody and misstates everyone's figures), post-submission attribution changes with their reasons, and the split-rule exceptions. The read files with the commission computation, and the two together are the payout's evidence.

lessons.title: Chapter 6 — Selling Settings
lessons.html:
The track's rules are enforced in configuration. This chapter walks the settings, each with its recommended posture and its control-register row.

1. The document chain settings.

1. Sales Order required — on for the invoice paths the policy gates: an invoice without an order is refused by configuration except for the named direct cases (module 7, Chapter 3). The setting turns the three-path rule from procedure into enforcement.
2. Delivery Note required — on where billing must follow despatch for stock items: performance before claim, enforced.
3. Both settings admit per-case exceptions only through the roles and lanes the site configures; the control register row states the posture and the exception owner.

2. The tolerance settings. The over-delivery and over-billing allowances (module 5, Chapter 4): the percentages, set low, with the exception role named. Register rows per the Inventory module 8 pattern — the setting, the value, the reason, the owner, the review date.

3. The customer and pricing defaults.

1. Customer naming — by name per the module 1 convention (naming series where the site prefers codes; the convention is the decision, the setting records it).
2. The default price list and territory — the fallback ends of the module 1-2 resolution chains: set once to the decided defaults, so the chain always resolves.
3. Maintain same rate throughout the sales cycle — the posture that holds rates consistent from order to invoice per the site's configuration: on per the standing recommendation, so rate changes route through amendments rather than drifting between documents.

4. The credit and stock interaction settings. The credit limit machinery's postures (module 1) and the reservation behaviour (module 4) read from their own configuration areas; this chapter's rule is the register's completeness: every setting that changes selling behaviour has a register row, whichever settings page it lives on — the quarterly confirmation pass (the Inventory track's control register review, extended) reads them all in one sitting.

5. Changing a setting. The governed-change procedure, restated for selling: the proposal with its reason, the owner's approval for postures that move money or controls, the change dated in the register, the affected procedures updated, and the change announced to the roles it touches. A settings change without its register row is the configuration drift the quarterly pass exists to catch.

6. The settings read — quarterly. The register against the live configuration: each row's stated value confirmed on screen, discrepancies investigated as either undocumented changes (the governance failure — closed by decision and record) or stale rows (updated). The pass rides the standing quarterly calendar with the access and stock reviews.

lessons.title: Chapter 7 — The consolidated selling calendar
lessons.html:
Modules 1-7 each installed reads on cadences. This chapter assembles them into the selling function's operating calendar — the rhythm the track is run by.

1. Daily / per run.

1. The invoicing run's two worklists — delivered-not-billed and due milestones — worked to zero (module 7).
2. Payments recorded same-day and allocated per remittances (module 7).
3. Despatch verifications and acknowledgments per despatch (module 5).

2. Weekly.

1. The fifteen-minute five-check read — open quotations, overdue rows, delivered-not-billed, discounts, the trend read — with the written note (module 6).
2. The delivery planning read — the coming window, overdue rows, at-risk rows (module 4).
3. The pending-acknowledgment read (module 5).
4. The collections gear worklist with promise dates (module 7).
5. The unallocated receipts read (module 7).
6. The order book pass, top-down by value (module 4).
7. The validity read on open quotations (module 3).

3. Monthly.

1. The conversion read and the deviations read (module 3).
2. The amendments read (module 4).
3. The returns read and the despatch sample (module 5).
4. The discounts read (module 6).
5. The credit changes, duplicate-candidate, and gate sample reads (module 1).
6. The price changes and completeness reads, and the rules read (module 2).
7. The bundle, blanket consumption, and attribution reads (this module).
8. The receivables summary and gear outcomes (module 7).
9. The monthly commercial review — the owner's session from the weekly notes and the monthly reads, closing with decisions entered into the governed lanes (module 6).

4. Quarterly.

1. The classification and hygiene reads on the customer register (module 1).
2. The item tax read with the accountant (module 2).
3. The deviation-versus-outcome read (module 3).
4. The cancellations and closures read (module 4).
5. The transit-damage read (module 5).
6. The bundle register review, and the settings register pass (this module).
7. The credit review on top exposures (module 1).

5. Annually. The terms templates review with counsel (module 3); the price architecture read (module 2); the full credit pass riding the receivables year-end (module 1); the policy set — ladders, postures, tolerances — reviewed and re-issued.

6. The calendar's filing. Every read files where its module stated; the weekly notes and monthly review minutes are the connective record. The calendar is deliberately the same shape as the Inventory track's — daily accuracy, weekly execution, monthly money, quarterly structure — so one operating rhythm serves the whole business.

lessons.title: Chapter 8 — Worked example: the Pharmacy Display Pack
lessons.html:
This chapter applies Chapters 2-6 to the standing case. Configuration values and outcomes are listed per step.

Step 1 — the bundle defined (Chapter 2). HealthTrade sells a retail setup package to pharmacy customers: four display shelves and one barcode scanner. The components' individual list prices total ₦450,000; the package's decided price is ₦361,000 — a 19.8% package reduction against component list, recorded with its arithmetic in the bundle register entry. The Product Bundle record creates: the parent item PHARM-DISPLAY-PACK (sales item, Maintain Stock off), the child table — 4 × display shelf, 1 × scanner — and the print description stating the contents. The bundle price loads onto the lists by the governed update.

Step 2 — the boundary confirmed (Chapter 2). The register entry records why this is a bundle and not production: the components remain ordinary stock until despatch and are gathered at picking; nothing called a display pack ever sits in the warehouse. The scanner remains individually sellable; the shelf remains a component and an item.

Step 3 — a bundle sale walked (Chapters 2-3). A pharmacy customer orders two packs:

1. The order — one row, PHARM-DISPLAY-PACK, quantity 2, at ₦361,000 each; the packed-items detail lists 8 shelves and 2 scanners; the availability check runs per component and passes.
2. The delivery — the pick list carries the components; the two scanners' serials capture at pick; the second-person check verifies ten physical units against the packed detail; stock deducts per component at submission.
3. The invoice — one line, quantity 2, at the bundle price: the customer's document states what the customer bought. Margin reads bundle revenue against the components' summed costs.

Step 4 — the blanket arrangement (Chapter 4). BizRetail Ltd negotiates a standing consumables arrangement for its branches: agreed quantities and rates for the year, approved at the arrangement's full value through the ladder. The Blanket Order records the items, quantities, rates, and period. Monthly call-offs run as Sales Orders against it — rates drawing from the arrangement without renegotiation, each call-off flowing through the standard commitment-delivery-invoice chain. The consumption read tracks drawdown; at month nine the read shows consumption ahead of run rate, and the renewal conversation opens before the arrangement exhausts.

Step 5 — attribution and the register rows (Chapters 5-6). The account's standing owner pre-fills the sales team section on both flows; the bundle launch is a split deal per the written split rules, entered at the order. The settings register gains its selling rows this quarter: Sales Order required on (direct cases named), Delivery Note required on, over-delivery tolerance at the low posture, same-rate-through-cycle on — each with owner, reason, and review date, confirmed at the quarterly pass.

The track closes. The selling function now runs end to end on registers, documents, and reads: customers gated, prices governed, offers versioned, commitments scheduled, despatches verified, invoices claiming what documents support, money allocated, and the calendar keeping all of it read. The Procurement track applies the same construction to the buying side.

lessons.title: Chapter 9 — Common errors and the module rule
lessons.html:
The errors that recur with the advanced instruments, each with its correction and prevention.

Error 1 — the stocked bundle. Symptom: the bundle parent created as a stock item; phantom balances nobody can count; reconciliations chasing an item that never physically exists. Correction: the parent corrected to non-stock through the lifecycle procedure; balances resolved. Prevention: Maintain Stock off on bundle parents, and the boundary test at definition.

Error 2 — the hand-assembled package. Symptom: packages sold as component lists at improvised prices; inconsistent package pricing across documents; the customer's invoice not stating what they bought. Correction: the bundle defined and priced by the governed update. Prevention: recurring packages are bundles by definition, per the register.

Error 3 — the bundle sold against a short component. Symptom: bundle orders accepted while a component is out of stock; waves failing at picking on the constraining component. Correction: the availability arithmetic applied; the wave re-dated or the component expedited. Prevention: the per-component availability check at order time.

Error 4 — the expired arrangement still pricing. Symptom: call-offs at blanket rates after the period ended; rate protection extended by inattention. Correction: the call-offs re-priced per current lists or a renewed arrangement. Prevention: the consumption read's expiry proximity, and the rule that a call-off after expiry is a new negotiation.

Error 5 — attribution adjusted at payout. Symptom: sales team sections edited after the fact to move commission; payout disputes; figures nobody trusts. Correction: attribution restored to the order's record; changes reviewed through the amendments discipline. Prevention: attribution set at the order, the integrity rule, and the monthly read listing post-submission changes.

Error 6 — the unregistered setting. Symptom: selling behaviour changed by a settings edit no register row records; the quarterly pass finding live values the register does not state. Correction: the change closed by decision and record, or reverted. Prevention: every behaviour-changing setting a register row, changed only by the governed procedure.

Review list. Before the quiz, confirm you can: define a bundle with the non-stock parent, the child table, and the boundary test; state the three document behaviours and the availability arithmetic; operate bundle returns and the register review; create and govern blanket orders with call-offs and the consumption read; configure attribution with the integrity rule and operate the commission boundary; walk the Selling Settings with their register rows; and run the consolidated calendar.

Module rule 8: the advanced instruments are registers with owners — bundles defined once with non-stock parents and decided arithmetic, arrangements holding negotiated terms for their period only, attribution stating who actually sold, and every behaviour-changing setting carrying its register row — operated inside the same document disciplines as the rest of the track. This completes the Selling track; the Procurement track covers the buying side.
